overall_summary: Analysis of 20 unique Shorts reveals that cosmic anomalies and bizarre animal biology are the primary growth drivers for FACTVERSE. Space-themed videos featuring sensory or physical paradoxes (e.g., burning ice, space oceans) consistently capture the highest views, while cognitive psychology and brain-related facts struggle to generate initial traction.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'The Planet of Burning Ice' achieved 577 views and 'The Largest Ocean in Space' hit 460 views, showing strong audience pull for extreme physics.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on space topics that present a physical impossibility or sensory contradiction in the hook.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'Sharks Are Older Than Trees' reached 302 views and 'This Animal Literally Dies Every Winter' hit 179 views.
winning_patterns.action: Create content around shocking animal survival mechanisms and historical biological timelines.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' (5 and 54 views) and 'The Real Reason Songs Get Stuck In Your Head' (17 views) underperformed significantly.
weak_patterns.action: Pivot away from abstract mental processes and reframe brain facts around tangible physical effects or technology.

next_video.reason: Leverages the high-performing 'Space Paradox' formula seen in the channel's top video (Planet of Burning Ice, 577 views) using a strong visual hook to boost retention.

experiment: Compare a visual-first hook (starting with 2 seconds of pure black screen and silence) against standard voiceover-first hooks to measure its impact on the 3-second view-vs-swipe-away ratio.
